title: Machine learning prediction of incident type 2 diabetes from electronic health records
abstract: We developed a gradient boosting model on longitudinal electronic health records from 48200 adults to predict incident type 2 diabetes within five years. Using routine laboratory values including HbA1c, fasting glucose, lipids, body mass index and blood pressure, the model achieved strong discrimination and was validated on an external primary care cohort.

title: Early detection of type 2 diabetes using random forest on routine clinical data
abstract: This study applies random forest classification to routine clinical measurements from 15600 adult patients to detect undiagnosed type 2 diabetes. Feature importance analysis identified fasting glucose, HbA1c, age and body mass index as the strongest predictors, and the model outperformed conventional risk scores.

title: Deep learning models for predicting type 2 diabetes onset from retinal fundus images
abstract: We trained a convolutional neural network on retinal fundus photographs from 28000 adults to estimate the risk of developing type 2 diabetes. The model learned vascular features associated with early metabolic change and predicted onset up to four years before clinical diagnosis.

title: XGBoost-based risk prediction of type 2 diabetes in a primary care cohort
abstract: A gradient boosting model was built from primary care records of 21400 adults aged 40 to 70 years to predict new onset type 2 diabetes. The model used demographic, anthropometric and laboratory predictors and showed good calibration across age and sex subgroups.

title: A machine learning approach to early screening for undiagnosed type 2 diabetes using NHANES data
abstract: Using nationally representative survey data from 9800 adults, we compared logistic regression, support vector machines and random forest for screening undiagnosed type 2 diabetes. The best model combined HbA1c, waist circumference and family history to identify undiagnosed cases with high sensitivity.

title: Predicting type 2 diabetes five years before onset with wearable sensor data and gradient boosting
abstract: We used continuous activity, heart rate and sleep data from wrist wearables worn by 3200 adults together with clinical variables to predict type 2 diabetes five years before diagnosis. Gradient boosting achieved earlier detection than models using clinical data alone.

title: Ensemble machine learning for early detection of type 2 diabetes in middle-aged adults
abstract: An ensemble of decision trees, logistic regression and neural networks was trained on health examination data from 18900 middle-aged adults to detect early type 2 diabetes. The ensemble improved recall compared with single models while keeping false positives low.

title: Interpretable machine learning for population screening of type 2 diabetes risk
abstract: We built an interpretable machine learning model using SHAP explanations on population health survey data from 12400 adults to screen for type 2 diabetes risk. The model highlights the contribution of glucose, age, body mass index and blood pressure to each individual risk estimate.

title: Neural network prediction of prediabetes progression to type 2 diabetes
abstract: A feedforward neural network was trained on 7600 adults with prediabetes to predict progression to type 2 diabetes within three years. Baseline HbA1c, fasting glucose, triglycerides and body mass index were the most informative predictors of progression.

title: A validated machine learning model for early identification of type 2 diabetes in community health screening
abstract: We developed and externally validated a machine learning screening tool for type 2 diabetes using community health screening data from 15300 adults. The model uses only low-cost measurements available in community settings and identifies high-risk adults who would benefit from confirmatory testing.

title: Machine learning prediction of type 1 diabetes onset in children and adolescents
abstract: We trained machine learning models on genetic markers and autoantibody measurements from 4100 children to predict the onset of type 1 diabetes. The model distinguished children who progressed to clinical type 1 diabetes from those who remained healthy.

title: Machine learning for glycaemic control in adults with established type 2 diabetes
abstract: This study uses reinforcement learning to optimise insulin dosing and glycaemic control in adults already diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. The model recommends dose adjustments based on continuous glucose monitoring data and meal records.

title: Deep learning for automated grading of diabetic retinopathy severity
abstract: A convolutional neural network was developed to grade diabetic retinopathy from fundus images of patients already diagnosed with diabetes. The system classifies retinopathy severity to prioritise ophthalmology referrals.

title: Machine learning prediction of coronary heart disease from electronic health records
abstract: We built a random forest model on electronic health records from 67000 adults to predict incident coronary heart disease. Predictors included cholesterol, blood pressure, smoking status and family history.

title: Machine learning models for early detection of chronic kidney disease
abstract: Gradient boosting and neural networks were trained on laboratory data from 23000 adults to detect chronic kidney disease at an early stage. Estimated glomerular filtration rate and albuminuria were the strongest predictors.

title: Epidemiology of type 2 diabetes prevalence in South Asian adults: a cross-sectional analysis
abstract: We report the prevalence and demographic distribution of type 2 diabetes in a cross-sectional survey of 8900 adults. The analysis describes associations with age, urban residence and socioeconomic status but does not develop any predictive model.

title: Machine learning in diabetes care: a systematic review of methods and applications
abstract: This systematic review summarises 84 studies applying machine learning to diabetes diagnosis, management and complication prediction. We synthesise methods, datasets and reported performance across the field.

title: Machine learning classification of diabetes in a mouse model of metabolic disease
abstract: We applied support vector machines to metabolic and transcriptomic data from diabetic mouse models to classify disease state. The study demonstrates proof of concept in animals only.

title: Machine learning prediction of gestational diabetes from first trimester data
abstract: A machine learning model was developed to predict gestational diabetes in 5600 pregnant women using first trimester clinical and laboratory measurements. The model supports early intervention during pregnancy.

title: Machine learning detection of type 2 diabetes in adolescents using school health data
abstract: We trained classification models on school health screening data from 9800 adolescents to detect type 2 diabetes in young people. The study focuses on a paediatric population.

title: Machine learning prediction of diabetes complications in patients with established type 2 diabetes
abstract: A model was developed to predict the development of neuropathy, nephropathy and cardiovascular events in 12000 patients already living with type 2 diabetes. The study addresses complication risk rather than initial detection.

title: A traditional risk score for type 2 diabetes based on the Framingham cohort
abstract: We derived a clinical risk score for type 2 diabetes using logistic regression on the Framingham cohort of 5200 adults. The score uses age, body mass index, blood pressure and family history without any machine learning algorithm.

title: Machine learning prediction of hypertension onset in a general adult population
abstract: Gradient boosting was applied to health examination data from 31000 adults to predict new onset hypertension. The model identifies adults at high risk of developing high blood pressure.

title: Deep learning detection of diabetic foot ulcers from thermal imaging
abstract: A convolutional neural network was trained on thermal images of feet from 2400 diabetic patients to detect foot ulcers. The tool supports wound care in patients already diagnosed with diabetes.

title: Machine learning prediction of COVID-19 severity in patients with diabetes
abstract: We built a model to predict severe COVID-19 outcomes among 6800 hospitalised patients with diabetes. Predictors included age, HbA1c, comorbidities and inflammatory markers.

title: Machine learning optimisation of insulin dosing for type 1 diabetes
abstract: A reinforcement learning system was developed to recommend insulin doses for 850 patients with type 1 diabetes using continuous glucose monitoring data. The study focuses on treatment optimisation.

title: Machine learning prediction of obesity from dietary and lifestyle data
abstract: Random forest and gradient boosting models were trained on dietary, activity and demographic data from 19000 adults to predict obesity. The study targets weight status rather than diabetes.

title: Machine learning classification of metabolic syndrome in middle-aged adults
abstract: We used machine learning to classify metabolic syndrome from clinical and laboratory data of 11000 adults. The outcome is a syndrome cluster, not type 2 diabetes onset.

title: Machine learning prediction of diabetic nephropathy progression
abstract: A model was built to predict progression of diabetic nephropathy in 9400 patients already diagnosed with diabetes and early kidney damage. The study addresses disease progression after diagnosis.

title: Genomic machine learning for diabetes risk in a paediatric cohort
abstract: We applied machine learning to genomic data from 3200 children to estimate genetic risk of diabetes. The study population is children and the outcome is genetic risk rather than clinical detection in adults.

title: Machine learning screening for depression in adults with diabetes
abstract: A natural language processing model was applied to clinical notes to screen for depression among 7800 adults with diabetes. The outcome is a mental health condition, not diabetes detection.

title: Machine learning prediction of hospital readmission in patients with diabetes
abstract: We trained a model on discharge records of 15400 patients with diabetes to predict 30-day hospital readmission. The study addresses health service use after diagnosis.

title: Deep learning detection of melanoma from dermoscopic images
abstract: A convolutional neural network was trained on 26000 dermoscopic images to detect melanoma skin cancer. The study addresses dermatology and is unrelated to diabetes.

title: Machine learning prediction of Alzheimer disease from brain imaging
abstract: We developed a deep learning model on magnetic resonance imaging data from 5400 older adults to predict Alzheimer disease. The study addresses neurodegenerative disease.

title: Machine learning prediction of sepsis in intensive care patients
abstract: A real-time machine learning model was developed to predict sepsis onset in 18000 intensive care patients using vital signs and laboratory values. The study addresses acute care.

title: Machine learning prediction of asthma exacerbations in adults
abstract: Gradient boosting was applied to electronic health records from 27000 adults with asthma to predict exacerbations. The study addresses respiratory disease.
